This issue might be a duplicate of existing issues. Please check:
- #40391: Same symptom — `@` file mention only shows directory names, never file names, with root cause analysis and suggested fix already provided.

Adding data from a headless `opencode run` setup, since the thread asked for a tool-to-stream lifecycle trace. Two things here that I don't think are in the issue yet: the hang is measurable as a rate rather than an anecdote, and the parent declares the session **idle** while a `task` fiber is still outstanding.

**Environment:** opencode 1.15.6, Linux, `opencode run --agent plan` non-interactive (stdin prompt, `--format default`), OpenRouter provider, models `z-ai/glm-5.2` and `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash`.

### The parent goes idle with a tool call still `running`

On a run that hung, the last assistant message had three `task` calls recorded as:

```
['completed', 'running', 'completed']
```

Roughly a minute later the log showed the loop finishing normally:

```
service=session.prompt session.id=ses_XXX step=6 loop
service=session.prompt session.id=ses_XXX exiting loop
service=bus type=session.idle publishing
service=bus type=session.diff publishing
```

No error, no warning, no abort. The session was declared idle with one `task` fiber never settled, no final assistant message was produced, and the process then stayed alive for a further **28 minutes** until my own wall-clock timeout SIGTERM'd it. From the caller's side the command emits nothing at all and looks like a 30-minute hang.

That matches the `awaitToolFibers` analysis above: if the stream succeeds but a tool fiber never settles, nothing bounds the wait. It also lines up with #17516 and #31109, which report the process-never-exits half of the same shape.

### It's measurable, and it isn't one model

Every `task` call opencode has ever recorded locally, from the session DB:

| Model | task calls | never returned | rate |
|---|---|---|---|
| `deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash` | 29 | 12 | **41%** |
| `z-ai/glm-5.2` | 12 | 2 | **17%** |

**Every one of those hung calls is terminal**: zero further messages in that session afterwards. That's worth stating because a stuck `running` row could otherwise just be an artifact of killing the process. These aren't. In the case above, opencode itself declared the session idle 28 minutes *before* anything killed it.

The apparent model split looks like frequency of use rather than an incompatibility. GLM hangs less because it delegates less, not because it's immune, so a report from one model won't reproduce reliably on another.

Anyone can get their own numbers against `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`:

```python
import sqlite3, json, collections
c = sqlite3.connect("file:opencode.db?mode=ro", uri=True); c.row_factory = sqlite3.Row
model = {}
for m in c.execute("select id,data from message"):
    d = json.loads(m["data"])
    if d.get("role") == "assistant":
        model[m["id"]] = str(d.get("modelID") or d.get("model") or "?")
hung, ok = collections.Counter(), collections.Counter()
for p in c.execute("select message_id,data from part"):
    pd = json.loads(p["data"])
    if pd.get("type") != "tool" or pd.get("tool") != "task":
        continue
    md = model.get(p["message_id"], "?")
    (hung if pd.get("state", {}).get("status") == "running" else ok)[md] += 1
for md in sorted(set(hung) | set(ok)):
    h, o = hung[md], ok[md]
    print(f"{md:<32}{h:>5} hung {o:>5} returned {h/(h+o)*100:>5.0f}%")
```

### Why the rate matters more than it looks

One hung subagent loses the whole run, not just its own slice, so a parent survives only if every call returns. At the rates above, three `task` calls come out around 21% and 57%. A run of mine that issued seven had roughly a 2% chance of returning anything.

### Workaround

Denying the `task` tool for the agent makes the model do the work inline:

```json
{ "agent": { "plan": { "permission": { "task": "deny" } } } }
```

Same model, same prompt, previously hung twice and then completed with a full result. Costs the parallelism and the per-subagent context window, so it's a stopgap rather than a fix, but a headless run that always returns beats one that returns nothing a third of the ti

## 详细日志分析（来自 debug 日志包 opencode-debug-20260804T173459.zip）

这是 **v1.18.13** 在 Windows 11 上的冻结事件日志分析。不是普通的 ResizeObserver 卡顿——有新的证据链。

---

### 完整时间线（北京时间 UTC+8）

| 时间 | 事件 | 证据文件 |
|------|------|----------|
| 01:27:35 | OpenCode Desktop v1.18.13 启动，sidecar 127.0.0.1:52076 | main.log |
| 01:27:40 | ResizeObserver loop 错误开始（零星） | renderer.log |
| 01:32:35-51 | 最后一次 agent 运行（run c618cfc4，16步），多次 rpm exhausted 流式错误被重试吞掉 | opencode.log |
| 01:32:57-33:02 | ResizeObserver 错误爆炸：5秒内 25+ 条 | renderer.log |
| 01:33:04 | 服务端正常 exiting loop，会话结束 | opencode.log |
| 01:34:31 | 最后一条 ResizeObserver 错误 | renderer.log |
| **01:34:51** | **渲染进程无响应** | window.log |
| 01:34:54 | 渲染进程恢复（约3秒） | window.log |
| 01:34:59 | 用户导出 debug 日志 | main.log |

---

### 关键证据 1：stack trace 精确卡死位置

window.log 在冻结时捕获的调用栈样本：

```
at computeTransform (main-5RU9uMOP.js:141619:28)
at computeStyle (main-5RU9uMOP.js:141615:18)
  at runComputation (main-5RU9uMOP.js:487:22)
  at updateComputation (main-5RU9uMOP.js:470:3)
  at runTop (main-5RU9uMOP.js:566:7)
  at runUserEffects (main-5RU9uMOP.js:660:39)
  at completeUpdates (main-5RU9uMOP.js:634:18)
  at runUpdates (main-5RU9uMOP.js:584:5)
  at batch (main-5RU9uMOP.js:265:10)
  at setStore (main-5RU9uMOP.js:34534:5)
```

**结论：** setStore 触发了 SolidJS 的批量响应式更新，computeTransform->computeStyle 的依赖图太大，单次同步批处理占满主线程 3 秒。

---

### 关键证据 2：rpm exhausted 作为放大器

服务端日志显示在冻结前 2 分钟，sensenova/deepseek-v4-flash 连续触发 rpm exhausted 错误：

```
17:32:35.295 ERROR stream error: "AI_APICallError: rpm exhausted"
17:32:37.304 自动重试成功
17:32:45.761 ERROR stream error: "AI_APICallError: rpm exhausted"
17:32:47.856 ERROR stream error: "AI_APICallError: rpm exhausted"
17:32:51.857 最终重试成功
```

每次重试意味着新的流式 token 被推入 store，每次 setStore 触发一次响应式 cascade。API 限流错误 -> 重试 -> 更多 store 写入 -> 更大的响应式依赖图 -> 更长的冻结时间。

---

### 关键证据 3：布局抖动（layout thrash）的量化数据

renderer.log 中 ResizeObserver loop completed with undelivered notifications 的数量：

- 本次会话（172735）：67 条，其中 5 秒内爆发 25+ 条
- 历史会话（125031）：约 20 条
- 更早会话（101628）：约 12 条

这是反复出现的慢性问题，每次会话都有，但严重程度在累积。

---

### 关键证据 4：异常大的 network.netlog（8.4 MB）

7 分钟会话产生 8.4 MB 网络日志，说明大量 IPC 流量涌入 UI（主要是流式 token + 工具结果逐 chunk 推入 store）。每次推送触发响应式更新，开销放大。

---

### 为什么这不是完全重复（与现有 issue 的区别）

| 现有 issue | 缺失的证据 | 本 issue 新增 |
|------------|-----------|--------------|
| #38296 | 只有 ResizeObserver 症状，无 stack trace | 精确的 computeTransform->computeStyle->setStore 调用链 |
| #37997 | 旧布局 UI 冻结，无 API 层关联 | 证明了 rpm exhausted 重试风暴与冻结的因果关系 |
| #33712 | 没有量化布局抖动频率 | 67 条 ResizeObserver 错误，爆发密度 5 秒 25+ 条 |
| #31099 | findDOMIndex 无限循环 | 不同路径——computeStyle 依赖图太大而非 DOM 索引循环 |

**本 issue 核心贡献：** 首次用 stack trace 证据链证明 setStore->SolidJS 响应式重算->computeStyle 是冻结的直接原因，并量化了 rpm exhausted 重试风暴作为放大器。

---

### 建议修复路径

1. **[高优先级] store 写入节流**：流式 token 入 store 时做 requestAnimationFrame 合并 + 阈值控制，避免逐 chunk 同步写入。这是最直接的缓解。
2. **[高优先级] ResizeObserver 防抖**：给虚拟列表的尺寸观测加 rAF 延迟 + size-delta 阈值，消除布局抖动死循环。
3. **[中优先级] 会话消息懒渲染**：16 步 + 大工具输出的会话消息树很大，考虑对历史消息做卸载或虚拟化。
4. **[低优先级] computeStyle bailout**：当 diff 为空时跳过全量重算。
5. **[低优先级] API 重试风暴保护**：rpm exhausted 重试时增加指数退避 + store 写入合并，减少重试对 UI 的冲击。

---

Additional official evidence from DeepSeek's changelog (https://api-docs.deepseek.com/updates):

> The two legacy API model names, deepseek-chat and deepseek-reasoner, will be discontinued in three months (2026-07-24). During the current period, these two model names point to the non-thinking mode and thinking mode of deepseek-v4-flash, respectively.

Two takeaways: these names were never separate models — just aliases for `deepseek-v4-flash` modes — and the 2026-07-24 discontinuation date has now passed, so they are fully retired. This supports removing the stale catalog entries (or marking them `deprecated`) so `/models` stops listing dead aliases alongside the real models.

Fourth independent confirmation, and I can now retract my own original diagnosis.

I filed this report. My investigation pointed at `models.dev` (an ESTABLISHED-but-idle TCP connection during init), and the duplicate-detection bot above followed that lead. **That was the wrong trail.** @JazielGuerrero and @zealchou have the actual cause, and I reproduced their determinism test on a platform not yet in this thread.

## Repro on macOS / arm64

Same two arms as @zealchou, unchanged:

```bash
# A — stdin is a pipe whose write end is never closed
mkfifo oc.fifo
sleep 120 > oc.fifo &
timeout 45 opencode run "answer in one word: what is 1+1?" < oc.fifo

# B — same command, stdin redirected to /dev/null
timeout 45 opencode run "answer in one word: what is 1+1?" < /dev/null
```

| Arm | Result |
|---|---|
| **A** | **5/5 hung.** `exit=124` every time, 45s wall clock, **0 bytes on stdout** |
| **B** | **6/6 succeeded.** `exit=0`, 2–37s (first run slower — model load) |

Not probabilistic. Deterministic in both directions.

| | |
|---|---|
| opencode | **1.18.5** |
| OS / arch | macOS 26.6, **arm64 (Apple silicon)** |
| Provider | local Ollama (`qwen3-coder:30b`) over the OpenAI-compatible endpoint |

Worth noting the version: @zealchou measured **1.18.10**, I measured **1.18.5**, on a different OS, different arch, and a different local-inference stack. Same trigger, so this is not recent and not platform-specific.

## Why my original "intermittent, 8–77% by hour" numbers fit this

My report described a failure rate that swung wildly by time of day. Measured then:

| Hour block | Success |
|---|---|
| 01–09 | 10/13 (77%) |
| 10 | 4/9 (44%) |
| 11–12 | 1/13 (8%) |
| 13 | 0/4 (0%) |
| 14–15 | 12/22 (55%) |
| **Total** | **27/61 (44%)** |

I treated the swing as a property of the environment. Under the stdin explanation it is a property of **how each batch was launched**, and one observation I could never explain now falls out cleanly:

> After 6 consecutive hangs, I built a controlled 40-run alternating A/B experiment to test an unrelated hypothesis (an offline env var). It ran **40/40 success over 42 minutes**, starting ~10 minutes after that failure streak, **with no configuration change whatsoever.** Both arms were 20/20, so the experiment was inconclusive by its own declared criterion — I recorded it as "cannot discriminate."

The thing that changed was not the config. It was that the 40 runs were driven by a purpose-built shell harness rather than the launcher used before it. Under @zealchou's explanation, that harness handed `opencode run` a stdin that reached EOF, so every run completed.

**Caveat, stated plainly:** I did not record the stdin state of each run at the time, so I cannot retroactively prove which launcher each of those 61 runs used. This is consistency with the hypothesis, not independent proof of it. The 5/5 vs 6/6 above is the proof; this section is just the anomaly that no longer needs a special explanation.

## Workaround

`< /dev/null` on every non-interactive invocation. Confirmed here.

## On the suggested fix

@zealchou's option 1 — skip the stdin read entirely when a prompt was already passed as an argument — would have prevented every failure I logged. In all 61 of my runs the prompt was supplied as an argument, so nothing was ever going to be merged in from stdin; the read was pure cost.

I would add one thing regardless of which option is chosen: **the failure mode itself is worth fixing separately.** No output, no error, no session, no log line past `message=init`, and an exit only when something external kills it. That is what turned a one-line stdin bug into a multi-day investigation that produced a wrong root cause. A bounded read that logged `stdin: waiting for EOF` even once would have ended it in minutes.

Happy to run further tests on macOS/arm64 if that helps.
